results.term_definition: Leo, "the Lion", is a constellation in the Zodiac, i.e. the stars that make up this constellation are in the part of the sky that intersects with the ecliptic (the plane defined by the Earth's path around the Sun). Hence, from our point of view here on Earth, we can regularly find the Sun, and also the other planets in our Solar System, in this constellation – in the case of the Sun from August 11 to September 17. (Of course if the Sun is there, we cannot see the constellation's stars.) In the night sky, Leo is easiest to observe in spring. It is one of the 88 modern constellations defined by the International Astronomical Union, and also one of the 48 classical constellations named by 2nd century astronomer Claudius Ptolemy. The brightest of Leo's numerous bright stars is called Regulus.
